questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman has a planned repeat cesarean delivery at 36 weeks' gestation. She has had three previous cesarean deliveries. Ultrasound during this pregnancy showed the placenta on the lower anterior wall, covering the internal cervical os and lying under the old scar. After the baby is delivered, the placenta does not separate from the uterine wall, and heavy bleeding begins. A hysterectomy is performed. Microscopy of the implantation site shows chorionic villi attached directly to the smooth muscle of the myometrium; the villi do not penetrate into the muscle layer. Which abnormality best explains this finding?
choices: Excess trophoblast growth from an all-paternal conceptus
Poor remodeling of the maternal spiral arteries
Absent or deficient decidua basalis at the implantation site
Early separation of a normally implanted placenta
Fetal vessels running in the membranes over the cervix
questions.explanation: Villi that touch the myometrium with **no decidua** between them define **placenta accreta**. The scar of a prior cesarean leaves a **deficient decidua basalis**, so the villi anchor directly to muscle and the placenta cannot separate after birth; a **previa over the scar** raises this risk greatly. Poor spiral artery remodeling is the tempting choice, but it is the defect of **preeclampsia**, where trophoblast invades too little, not too much. Abruption is separation that comes too early, not a failure to separate.
questions.explanation_pt: Vilosidades em contato com o miométrio **sem decídua** entre eles definem a **placenta acreta**. A cicatriz de uma cesárea prévia deixa uma **decídua basal deficiente**, então as vilosidades se prendem diretamente ao músculo e a placenta não se descola após o parto; uma **placenta prévia sobre a cicatriz** aumenta muito esse risco. O remodelamento deficiente das artérias espiraladas é a alternativa tentadora, mas é o defeito da **pré-eclâmpsia**, em que o trofoblasto invade de menos, e não de mais. O descolamento prematuro é uma separação precoce, e não uma falha em se separar.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 38 weeks' gestation is in active labor. She has had one previous vaginal delivery and no uterine surgery. Her membranes rupture, and bright red vaginal bleeding starts right away. She has no pain between contractions, and the uterus is soft between them. Blood pressure is 118/72 mm Hg and pulse is 84/min. The fetal heart rate was normal a few minutes earlier; it now falls to 80/min and stays low. An ultrasound at 20 weeks showed a placenta high on the posterior wall, far from the cervix, and an umbilical cord that inserted into the membranes instead of into the placenta. What is the most likely source of the bleeding?
choices: Fetal vessels running unprotected through the membranes
Placental tissue lying over the internal cervical os
Maternal vessels torn as the placenta separates early
A tear through a previous uterine scar
Cervical capillaries injured by rapid dilation
questions.explanation: Bleeding that starts when the **membranes rupture**, with a stable mother and a fetus that becomes **bradycardic** within minutes, suggests **vasa previa**. With a **velamentous cord insertion**, fetal vessels cross the membranes over the os and tear at rupture, so the lost blood is **fetal**, and a small volume is a large part of the fetal blood volume. Placenta previa also causes painless bright red bleeding, but this placenta was far from the os, and in previa the blood is maternal, so the fetus is usually stable at first. Abruption causes pain and a firm uterus, and a uterine scar is absent here.
questions.explanation_pt: Sangramento que começa na **ruptura das membranas**, com mãe estável e feto que evolui com **bradicardia** em minutos, sugere **vasa prévia**. Com **inserção velamentosa do cordão**, vasos fetais cruzam as membranas sobre o orifício e se rompem com a amniorrexe; o sangue perdido é **fetal**, e um volume pequeno representa grande parte da volemia fetal. A placenta prévia também causa sangramento indolor e vermelho vivo, mas esta placenta estava longe do orifício, e na prévia o sangue é materno, de modo que o feto costuma estar estável no início. O descolamento prematuro causa dor e útero endurecido, e aqui não há cicatriz uterina.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman in her first pregnancy comes for a visit at 33 weeks' gestation with headache and new swelling of her face and hands. Her blood pressure was 112/70 mm Hg at 12 weeks. Today, blood pressure is 162/104 mm Hg on two readings, urine dipstick shows 2+ protein, platelets are 165,000/μL, serum creatinine is 0.8 mg/dL, and AST is 28 U/L. Which change in her blood most directly causes injury to her vascular endothelium?
choices: Rise in free placental growth factor (PlGF)
Fall in plasma endothelin-1
Rise in placental prostacyclin release
Rise in endothelial nitric oxide production
Rise in soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1
questions.explanation: New hypertension with proteinuria after 20 weeks is **preeclampsia**. The poorly perfused placenta releases **soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1)**, a soluble **VEGF receptor** that binds VEGF and **PlGF** and takes them away from the maternal endothelium, which needs them to stay healthy; this causes hypertension and **proteinuria**. A rise in free PlGF is the tempting choice, but free PlGF actually **falls** because sFlt-1 binds it. In preeclampsia, endothelin rises while prostacyclin and nitric oxide fall, so the balance shifts toward vasoconstriction.
questions.explanation_pt: Hipertensão nova com proteinúria após 20 semanas é **pré-eclâmpsia**. A placenta mal perfundida libera **sFlt-1**, um **receptor solúvel de VEGF** que se liga ao VEGF e ao **PlGF** e os retira do endotélio materno, que depende deles para se manter saudável; isso causa hipertensão e **proteinúria**. O aumento do PlGF livre é a alternativa tentadora, mas o PlGF livre na verdade **cai**, porque o sFlt-1 se liga a ele. Na pré-eclâmpsia, a endotelina aumenta, enquanto a prostaciclina e o óxido nítrico diminuem, e o equilíbrio pende para a vasoconstrição.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman at 32 weeks' gestation has had pain in the upper abdomen, nausea and malaise for 1 day. Blood pressure is 148/96 mm Hg, pulse is 96/min, and temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F). She is tender in the epigastrium and right upper quadrant. She is alert and has no focal neurologic signs. Laboratory results: hemoglobin 9.6 g/dL, platelets 62,000/μL, AST 286 U/L, ALT 240 U/L, LDH 1,150 U/L, haptoglobin low, glucose 92 mg/dL, prothrombin time and fibrinogen normal, and creatinine 0.9 mg/dL. The blood smear shows schistocytes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
choices: Acute fatty liver of pregnancy
HELLP syndrome
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy
Disseminated intravascular coagulation
questions.explanation: **Hemolysis** (schistocytes, high LDH, low haptoglobin), **elevated liver enzymes** with right upper quadrant pain, and **low platelets** in the third trimester with hypertension define **HELLP syndrome**, a severe form of preeclampsia. Acute fatty liver of pregnancy is the tempting choice, but it is a form of liver failure with **hypoglycemia** and a **prolonged prothrombin time**; here glucose and PT are normal. DIC would prolong the PT and lower fibrinogen, cholestasis of pregnancy causes itching and high bile acids without hemolysis, and TTP (low ADAMTS13) does not usually cause this degree of liver injury, and it does not resolve with delivery.
questions.explanation_pt: **Hemólise** (esquizócitos, LDH alta, haptoglobina baixa), **enzimas hepáticas elevadas** com dor em hipocôndrio direito e **plaquetopenia** no terceiro trimestre, com hipertensão, definem a **síndrome HELLP**, forma grave de pré-eclâmpsia. A esteatose hepática aguda da gestação é a alternativa tentadora, mas é uma insuficiência hepática com **hipoglicemia** e **tempo de protrombina prolongado**; aqui a glicemia e o TP são normais. A CIVD prolongaria o TP e reduziria o fibrinogênio, a colestase intra-hepática da gestação causa prurido e ácidos biliares elevados sem hemólise, e a PTT (ADAMTS13 baixa) não costuma causar lesão hepática dessa intensidade nem regride com o parto.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 17 weeks' gestation has vaginal spotting. Ultrasound shows a live fetus that is small for its gestational age, with fused fingers (syndactyly) on both hands. The placenta is large and contains many small cystic spaces. Serum beta-hCG is mildly high for gestational age. Amniocentesis shows a fetal karyotype of 69,XXY. Which event at conception most likely produced this pregnancy?
choices: Fertilization of an ovum with no maternal chromosomes by one sperm whose genome duplicated
Nondisjunction of chromosome 21 during maternal meiosis I
Fertilization of a diploid ovum (failed maternal meiosis) by one sperm
Fertilization of a normal haploid ovum by two sperm
Mitotic nondisjunction in the early embryo after fertilization
questions.explanation: A fetus with growth restriction and syndactyly, a large cystic placenta, a mildly high hCG and a **triploid** karyotype describe a **partial hydatidiform mole**. It most often arises when a normal ovum is fertilized by **two sperm**, giving one maternal and **two paternal** chromosome sets; the maternal set allows fetal tissue to form, and the extra paternal set drives the swollen villi. An extra **maternal** set (diploid ovum) also gives triploidy, but it is linked to a small, non-molar placenta. Fertilization of an ovum with no maternal chromosomes produces a **complete mole**, which has no fetus.
questions.explanation_pt: Feto com restrição de crescimento e sindactilia, placenta grande e cística, hCG discretamente elevado e cariótipo **triploide** descrevem uma **mola hidatiforme parcial**. Na maioria das vezes surge quando um óvulo normal é fecundado por **dois espermatozoides**, resultando em um conjunto cromossômico materno e **dois paternos**; o conjunto materno permite a formação de tecido fetal, e o conjunto paterno extra causa o edema das vilosidades. Um conjunto **materno** extra (óvulo diploide) também causa triploidia, mas se associa a placenta pequena e não molar. A fecundação de um óvulo sem cromossomos maternos produz uma **mola completa**, que não tem feto.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman has had a cough for 3 weeks and has coughed up blood twice. Five months ago she delivered a healthy baby at term after a normal pregnancy, and since then she has had irregular vaginal bleeding. Chest x-ray shows many round nodules in both lungs. Serum beta-hCG is very high. Pelvic ultrasound shows a hemorrhagic mass in the uterine wall. A biopsy of one lung nodule most likely shows which finding?
choices: Malignant cyto- and syncytiotrophoblast with no chorionic villi
Swollen chorionic villi with trophoblast growing into vessels
Glomerulus-like structures (Schiller-Duval bodies)
Sheets of large clear cells with lymphocytes in septa
Nests of atypical squamous cells with keratin pearls
questions.explanation: A very high hCG, uterine bleeding and **lung metastases** after a pregnancy point to **gestational choriocarcinoma**, which spreads early through the **blood**. It is made of malignant **cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast** with hemorrhage and necrosis, and it has **no chorionic villi**. Invasive mole is the tempting choice: it can also reach the lungs, but it contains villi and follows a **molar** pregnancy, not a normal term birth. Schiller-Duval bodies belong to yolk sac tumor, and clear cells with lymphocytes to dysgerminoma.
questions.explanation_pt: hCG muito alto, sangramento uterino e **metástases pulmonares** após uma gestação indicam **coriocarcinoma gestacional**, que se dissemina precocemente pelo **sangue**. Ele é formado por **citotrofoblasto e sinciciotrofoblasto** malignos com hemorragia e necrose, e **não tem vilosidades coriônicas**. A mola invasora é a alternativa tentadora: também pode chegar aos pulmões, mas contém vilosidades e sucede uma gestação **molar**, e não um parto normal a termo. Corpúsculos de Schiller-Duval pertencem ao tumor do saco vitelino, e células claras com linfócitos ao disgerminoma.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman at 22 weeks' gestation has a uterus larger than expected for her dates. Ultrasound shows twins of the same sex with a single placenta and a thin membrane separating two amniotic sacs. One twin is large, has a full bladder and is surrounded by too much amniotic fluid. The other twin is small, has no visible bladder and has almost no amniotic fluid around it. Which best describes how and when these twins arose?
choices: Split of one embryo at days 0 to 4
Split of one embryo at days 4 to 8
Split of one embryo at days 8 to 12
Split of one embryo after day 13
Fertilization of two separate ova
questions.explanation: One placenta with a thin dividing membrane means **monochorionic, diamniotic** twins. Shared placental vessels connect their circulations, and an unbalanced flow causes **twin-twin transfusion**: the donor becomes hypovolemic and makes little urine (**oligohydramnios**), and the recipient becomes volume-overloaded and makes much urine (**polyhydramnios**). This pattern follows a split at **days 4 to 8**, after the chorion forms but before the amnion does. A split at days 8 to 12 is the tempting choice, but it gives **one amniotic sac** with no dividing membrane, and twins from two ova always have two chorions.
questions.explanation_pt: Uma placenta com membrana divisória fina significa gêmeos **monocoriônicos e diamnióticos**. Vasos placentários compartilhados conectam as duas circulações, e um fluxo desequilibrado causa a **síndrome de transfusão feto-fetal**: o doador fica hipovolêmico e produz pouca urina (**oligoidrâmnio**), e o receptor fica hipervolêmico e produz muita urina (**polidrâmnio**). Esse padrão resulta de uma divisão entre os **dias 4 e 8**, depois da formação do córion e antes da formação do âmnio. A divisão entre os dias 8 e 12 é a alternativa tentadora, mas gera **um único saco amniótico** sem membrana divisória, e gêmeos de dois óvulos sempre têm dois córions.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman at 35 weeks' gestation is brought to the hospital after a generalized seizure at home. She had no history of seizures or kidney disease, and her blood pressure was normal early in pregnancy. Blood pressure is now 174/112 mm Hg, and urine dipstick shows 3+ protein. A second seizure follows, and CT shows a large intracerebral hemorrhage. She dies despite treatment. At autopsy, which kidney finding is most likely?
choices: Subepithelial immune deposits forming spikes along the basement membrane
Normal glomeruli on light microscopy with podocyte foot process effacement
Swollen glomerular endothelial cells that narrow the capillary lumens
Crescents of proliferating cells filling Bowman space
Nodular expansion of the mesangial matrix
questions.explanation: New severe hypertension, heavy proteinuria and seizures in late pregnancy are **eclampsia**. The typical kidney lesion of preeclampsia and eclampsia is **glomerular endotheliosis**: swollen glomerular **endothelial cells** that narrow the capillary lumens, reflecting the loss of VEGF support to the endothelium; it usually reverses after delivery. Minimal change disease is the tempting choice for heavy proteinuria, but its glomeruli look normal on light microscopy. Spikes suggest membranous nephropathy, crescents a rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, and nodular mesangial expansion diabetic nephropathy.
questions.explanation_pt: Hipertensão grave nova, proteinúria intensa e convulsões no fim da gestação caracterizam a **eclâmpsia**. A lesão renal típica da pré-eclâmpsia e da eclâmpsia é a **endoteliose glomerular**: **células endoteliais** glomerulares edemaciadas que estreitam a luz dos capilares, refletindo a perda do suporte de VEGF ao endotélio; costuma regredir após o parto. A doença de lesões mínimas é a alternativa tentadora para proteinúria intensa, mas seus glomérulos parecem normais à microscopia óptica. *Spikes* sugerem nefropatia membranosa, crescentes uma glomerulonefrite rapidamente progressiva, e expansão nodular do mesângio a nefropatia diabética.
